standard.title: Spelling patterns and morphemes
standard.description: use knowledge of spelling patterns and morphemes to read and write words whose spelling is not completely predictable from their sounds, including high-frequency words
standard.prior_knowledge: Students spell one- and two-syllable words using common letter patterns, and read and write an increasing number of high-frequency words (AC9E1LY13/14). They have not yet applied morphemic knowledge to words with irregular or unpredictable sound-spelling relationships.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can use spelling patterns and morphemes to read and write words whose spelling is not completely predictable from their sounds, including high-frequency words.

nodes.label: Spelling patterns for irregular words
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply known spelling patterns to read and write words with unpredictable sound-spelling relationships.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply a known spelling pattern to write an irregular high-frequency word correctly (e.g. 'one', 'once').
nodes.typical_width: Apply spelling pattern knowledge to a range of irregular words and high-frequency words; use context to select the correct form when a word has more than one plausible pronunciation.
wider: Group irregular words by shared spelling pattern and discuss what the pattern reveals about English spelling history
Use context clues in a sentence to read a word with multiple plausible pronunciations (e.g. 'read' — present vs past tense)

response_modes.reason: Spelling irregular words correctly requires memorisation and pattern recognition built through repeated exposure and writing practice. Width is thin — the skill does not vary meaningfully across contexts. Repeated correct production in writing is the productive investment.

success_criteria: Student correctly spells a set of irregular high-frequency words in their writing.
Student can use context to select the correct pronunciation when a word is ambiguous.

nodes.label: Using morphemes to spell unknown words
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply morphemic knowledge — recognising base words, prefixes and suffixes — to spell unknown words by analogy with known words.
nodes.minimum_width: Use a known word to spell a related unknown word through morphemic analogy (e.g. use 'one' to spell 'once', use 'cover' to spell 'uncover').
nodes.typical_width: Apply morphemic knowledge across a range of word families — using base words and affixes to generate correct spellings of unknown words — in both isolated practice and writing contexts.
wider: Build a word family from a known base word and discuss how morphemic knowledge generalises to new words
Identify morphemic relationships between words encountered in learning area texts and use them to unlock unknown words during reading
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Building word families through morphemic analogy connects spelling to word meaning and vocabulary development — advancing students who explore morphemic relationships are building vocabulary knowledge simultaneously. This is genuinely productive richness within Year 2.
success_criteria: Student correctly spells an unknown word by applying morphemic knowledge from a known word.
Student can identify the morphemic relationship between a known and an unknown word.
